name: vscode-dataflex
description: DataFlex language support: syntax highlighting, outline, build and run.

dataflex.cliPath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to `df-cli.exe`. Leave empty to discover it from `PATH`, the registry, then the conventional `Program Files\DataFlex <version>` layout.

dataflex.workspaceFile.markdownDescription: Path to the `.sws` workspace file to use, relative to the folder root. Leave empty to detect it automatically; you will be prompted if a folder contains more than one.

dataflex.build.restartWebApp.markdownDescription: Pass `--restart-webapp` when building, stopping the matching WebApp Server application first and restarting it afterwards.

dataflex.trace.server.description: Trace communication with the DataFlex language server.

dataflex.test.timeoutSeconds.markdownDescription: How long to wait for a DFUnit test executable before terminating it. A program that opens a modal error dialog would otherwise never return.

dataflex.docs.baseUrl.markdownDescription: Base URL used for the documentation link in hovers. **Clear it to turn the links off.** Links are only ever produced for classes from the DataFlex runtime library and its packages -- your own classes are not in the documentation, so linking them would give a dead link. No network request is made: the URL is constructed from the class name and the package the class was declared in.

dataflex.inlayHints.parameterNames.markdownDescription: Show parameter names before the arguments of a `Send` or `Get`. DataFlex passes positionally with no punctuation, so a call like `Send PopupLookup Self "" "" ""` says nothing about what its arguments are. Off by default because hints are drawn inside the code; a name is only shown when every matching declaration agrees on it.

dataflex.inlayHints.suppressWhenArgument.markdownDescription: Hide a parameter hint when the argument already carries the parameter's name, so `sCustomerAccount: sCustomerAccount` is not drawn. Leaves calls where only some arguments differ showing only some hints, which can look as though the rest failed — turn this off to label every argument.

dataflex.hover.tableFields.markdownDescription: List a table's columns when hovering its name, instead of only counting them. Off by default because a table hover fires on every `Open` and every DDO line, and a wide table would fill the screen; the column list is read from the workspace's `.fd` files, so it costs nothing to turn on.

dataflex.analysis.unused-local.markdownDescription: Report local variables that are never read.

dataflex.analysis.unreachable-code.markdownDescription: Report statements that follow an unconditional `Procedure_Return` / `Function_Return`.

dataflex.analysis.duplicate-declaration.markdownDescription: Report a local name declared twice in the same scope.

dataflex.analysis.unused-parameter.markdownDescription: Report parameters that are never read. Overrides of a parent class member and empty event stubs are excluded, since accepting arguments you do not use is unavoidable there; what remains is hand-written code that genuinely ignores one.

dataflex.analysis.severity.markdownDescription: Severity for inline analysis findings. `hint` greys the code out but is **not listed in the Problems panel** (VS Code shows hints in the editor only). Raise it to `information` or `warning` to have findings listed. *DataFlex: Analyze Workspace* always lists its results regardless of this setting. A few rules carry a higher built-in default and ignore this -- `implicit-global` always reports as a warning unless `#dataflex.analysis.severityOverrides#` says otherwise.

dataflex.analysis.exclude.markdownDescription: Globs excluded from *DataFlex: Analyze Workspace*, e.g. `**/ChilkatAx*.pkg` for generated vendor wrappers. Empty by default so nothing is hidden silently; the report states how many files were skipped. To disable analysis from inside a file instead, put `// df-analysis-ignore` (or `// df-analysis-ignore: unused-local, dead-procedure`) anywhere in it.

dataflex.analysis.severityOverrides.markdownDescription: Severity for individual rules, overriding `#dataflex.analysis.severity#`. Useful when one rule is legitimately noisy: `{ "unused-local": "hint" }` keeps it greyed out in the editor while everything else is listed in the Problems panel.

dataflex.analysis.dead-procedure.markdownDescription: Report procedures and functions that nothing appears to call. **Workspace-only** -- it needs the whole index, so it is reported by *DataFlex: Analyze Workspace*, never live while typing. Off by default: DataFlex dispatches dynamically, so judge the false-positive rate on your own code before trusting it. Overrides of a parent class member, published methods, and any name appearing in a string literal are all treated as reachable.

dataflex.analysis.argument-count.markdownDescription: Report calls that pass the wrong number of arguments. **Workspace-only** -- it needs the whole index, so it is reported by *DataFlex: Analyze Workspace*, never live while typing. Reported at **warning** severity. DataFlex compiles a call with too few arguments and simply leaves them unset, so this catches a class of bug the compiler does not. It stays silent unless it is certain: the name must be declared in your own source, every declaration of it must agree on how many parameters it takes, and none may read `num_arguments` -- which is how DataFlex writes an optional parameter.

dataflex.coverage.exclude.markdownDescription: Globs left out of *Run with Coverage*. Only source reachable from the test program is instrumented in the first place, so this is for narrowing further -- `**/Tests/**` keeps the test code itself out of the percentage, since tests always run and otherwise flatter the figure. Empty by default so nothing is hidden silently; the run reports how many files were skipped.

dataflex.analysis.implicit-global.markdownDescription: Report a variable declared outside any procedure or function -- typically inside an `Object ... End_Object` body, where it looks like per-object state but is actually one program-wide global shared by every object. Reported at **warning** severity regardless of `#dataflex.analysis.severity#`, because it is a correctness hazard rather than untidiness; lower it with `#dataflex.analysis.severityOverrides#` if you disagree. The fix is a `Property` for object state, or `Global_Variable` to declare a global deliberately.

dataflex.preview.theme.markdownDescription: Theme *DataFlex: Preview Web View* draws with, e.g. `Df_Material`. Must be one of the folders in the workspace's `AppHtml\CssThemes`. Leave empty to use `Df_Flat_Desktop` where the workspace ships it, and whatever it does ship otherwise.

dataflex.debuggerProgId.markdownDescription: COM ProgID of the DataFlex debugger engine, e.g. `VDFDebugger.DebuggerEngine.26.0`. Leave empty to use the newest installed version. Present only in the debug build (`npm run package:debug`); see `docs/DEBUGGING.md`.

project.description: Project (.src) within the workspace. Defaults to the selected project.

program.description: The compiled program to debug. Defaults to the selected project's executable in the workspace's Programs directory.

project.description: Project to debug, when the workspace has more than one. Defaults to the one selected in the status bar.

cwd.description: Working directory. Defaults to the directory holding the .sws.

stopOnEntry.description: Break before the program starts running.

webApp.description: Debug as a web application. NOT WORKING YET: the engine still launches the program standalone, which stops on a modal dialog. See docs/DEBUGGING.md.

url.description: URL to open when webApp is set.

acceptNewWebAppSessions.description: Let an incoming web app session take over the session being debugged. Off by default, so a second browser tab cannot silently steal the session you are standing in.

noDebugHeap.description: Start the program without the debug heap.

processId.description: Process id of a running DataFlex program built with debug information.
